sources: SATURDAY Sep 26 2026 RUN (06:15 UTC, post-close). Markets shut; all figures are Friday Sep 25 closes unless dated otherwise. HEADLINE: the rates shock kept going even as risk assets relaxed. The 10y finished Sep 25 at 5.17 pct and the 2y at 4.81 pct (Advisor Perspectives/dshort Treasury Yields Snapshot, Sep 25), putting 2s10s at 0.36 - a fourth straight session of bear steepening and up 9bp from 0.27 in the last run. FRED's T10Y2Y is 0.31 dated Sep 24, so the 0.36 is one day fresher; either way the direction is unambiguous. RATES VOL - NEW PRINT: MOVE 104.58, its highest since March, per Fundstrat First to Market Sep 25 citing Thursday's close; Bloomberg the same morning headlined Treasury volatility set for its biggest jump in a year. That replaces last run's carried 95.45 and confirms the MEDIUM-LOW confidence call then was directionally right. MOVE is now up roughly 30 pct in a week. EQUITY VOL: VIX 15.22, -2.87 pct on the day (Schwab market update, Sep 25), versus 15.67 on Sep 24 and 14.81 on Sep 18 (Investing.com historical). So equity vol is UP about 3 pct week-over-week but fell on Friday. The divergence flagged in the last two runs is now extreme and has been picked up by the sell side: MOVE at a six-month high against a VIX in the low 15s. ENERGY - THE WEEK'S TURN: Brent 104.37, down 2.09 pct on Sep 25 (TradingEconomics), WTI 92.54 -2.34 pct. The fall is on reports of US-Iran talks over a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Brent is still +20 pct on the month and about +51 pct y/y, and still up week-over-week, so trend stays up, but the Hormuz premium started leaking out on Friday. This is the single biggest change in the risk picture versus yesterday. DOLLAR: DXY 101.03, -0.25 pct (TradingEconomics Sep 25; Schwab had 100.98 intraday). First down day after five up. Still higher than a week ago, trend up. COPPER/GOLD: copper 6.70 USD/lb (TradingEconomics Sep 25, -0.35 pct), gold spot 4,280.19 USD/oz (USAGOLD daily report Sep 25, +0.12 pct). Ratio 1.57, unchanged. Copper is holding near records while gold consolidates - still the cleanest pro-cyclical signal on the board. CREDIT - THE ONE THAT MOVED: HY OAS 280bp, FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 dated Sep 24 (2.80 pct), up from the 270 carried last run. That is the first real widening of this episode and it validates the warning from the previous two runs that credit had not repriced. 280 is the level flagged as the line to watch and it has been reached. Trend up, HIGH confidence - this is a dated FRED print, not an estimate. INFLATION EXPECTATIONS: 5y5y forward 2.34 pct on Sep 25 versus 2.35 on Sep 21 (FRED T5YIFR). Flat. Notably, breakevens are NOT confirming the oil spike - the 10y selloff is a real-rate/term-premium story, not an inflation-expectations story. CONSUMER - NEW PRINT: UMich final September 48.1, revised up from the 47.8 preliminary but down 7.0 pct from 51.7 in August and the lowest in four months, below the 1st percentile of the index's history (Advisor Perspectives, CNN, Conference/UMich Surveys of Consumers, released 10:00 ET Sep 25). Marked flat week-over-week because the 0.3 revision is noise; the real signal is the m/m collapse. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS: NFCI -0.555, week ending Sep 18 (Chicago Fed via FRED) - no new weekly print since the last run, still the loosest of the cycle. Flat. LABOR: initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 19 (DOL, released Sep 24), versus 201k consensus and 196k prior. No new release this run; next is Oct 1. Trend flat. CARRIED with no new releases: ISM manufacturing 54.6 (August, eighth straight month of expansion, next print Oct 1), building permits 1,403k (August, -2.1 pct m/m, trend down, next Oct 17), LEI y/y approx -0.7 pct (August LEI edged down), Sahm rule -0.07 (August, next Oct 2), SOFR-OIS 0bp and EUR/USD 3M xccy basis -10bp (standing assumptions, no free live source), global liquidity 1 (stable). BDTI DATA FLAG: carried at 4,899 for a SIXTH consecutive run. No dated Baltic print retrievable again - Investing.com still stale at 1,107 dated 31/03, MacroMicro returns 403, StockQ shows an empty table, Baltic Exchange is subscription-only. LOW CONFIDENCE; treat as non-informative until a paid or alternative source is wired in. PICTURE: four sessions into the rates shock and the pattern finally broke in two directions at once. Oil turned down on Hormuz de-escalation talk and the dollar had its first down day, which takes some pressure off. But the two things that had been conspicuously asleep started to wake: MOVE jumped to a six-month high and HY OAS widened 10bp to 280 - the exact threshold flagged as the tell. Meanwhile the 10y made another leg higher and the curve bear-steepened again. The read is that the bond market was not wrong and credit is now catching up, just slowly. Equity vol at 15.2 and NFCI at the loosest of the cycle remain the two holdouts. The domestic soft spots got worse, not better: UMich at 48.1 is a four-month low and a 7 pct monthly drop, LEI still negative y/y, permits falling. Claims at 197k still say no labor-market crack, which keeps the policy-error framing intact - the Fed has no cover to ease into a 5.17 pct 10y. WATCH: whether HY OAS pushes through 300, whether MOVE holds above 100, whether the Hormuz de-escalation is real or a headline fade, whether the 10y stalls at 5.25, ISM manufacturing Oct 1 and claims Oct 1. SOURCES: Advisor Perspectives/dshort (Treasury yields Sep 25, consumer sentiment Sep 25), Fundstrat First to Market Sep 25 (MOVE), Bloomberg Sep 25 (Treasury volatility), Charles Schwab market update Sep 25 (VIX, DXY, WTI, 10y), TradingEconomics (Brent, copper, DXY), USAGOLD daily report Sep 25 (gold), FRED/St. Louis Fed (T10Y2Y, T5YIFR, BAMLH0A0HYM2, NFCI), Chicago Fed, US Department of Labor, Census Bureau/HUD, Conference Board, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, ISM, CNN Business, Baltic Exchange.
